1) Primary label choice (ICT) is not well aligned with the model’s own candidate distribution, where TICT is slightly higher probability than ICT (0.392 vs 0.342 in mechanism_context), so the adjudication rationale needs to explicitly override that prior with strong target-side evidence rather than “slightly ahead” language.
2) The argument “strong gap decrease ⇒ ICT” is weakly grounded because the redistribution/dipole proxies are low and distributed (E35, E36; also low Δdipole in features_summary). A large Δgap (E32/E22) without localized charge rearrangement can also occur from geometric relaxation or packing-induced electronic changes; this keeps “neutral aromatic” more competitive than stated (E23, E35).
3) The torsion-based anti-TICT claim is directionally reasonable (very small Δdihedral, E31/E21), but the use of atb_dihedral_thresh_none=8° is likely miscalibrated relative to observed magnitudes (~0.03–0.07° in E21). That threshold comparison may be non-informative and should be replaced with within-dataset/neighbor-relative separation (E21, E24).
